sources.title: Climate
supported_paraphrases: SANParks groups April–September as dry winter and October–March as rainy summer.
Sparse winter vegetation and limited water can aid viewing; sightings remain uncertain.
Warm layers are appropriate for winter night drives.

sources.title: Vital information
supported_paraphrases: Visitors must stay inside vehicles except at designated areas.
Published limits are 50 km/h on tar and 40 km/h on gravel; gate times govern travel.
Off-road driving and feeding or disturbing animals are prohibited.

sources.title: Day visits
supported_paraphrases: Daily visitor capacity limits apply; advance day reservations are available.

sources.title: Visitor tips
supported_paraphrases: SANParks recommends modest driving distances with frequent stops.
Camp lighting is limited; a torch or headlamp is recommended.
Accommodation tariffs exclude meals; check unit facilities when booking.

sources.title: Game drives
supported_paraphrases: Guided morning drives begin before public gate opening.
Guided sunset drives return after sunset; these are distinct from private self-drive permission.

team_draft_corrections: Remove guaranteed visibility: neither seasons nor sightings are guarantees.
Use the operator seasonal bands April–September dry and October–March rainy, while explaining transition variability.
Do not claim summer automatically means cheaper accommodation, fewer crowds or easier travel without dated evidence.
Do not promise newborn wildlife, predictable shower duration or a single best month for every first-time visitor.
Do not infer winter eliminates malaria risk. Park malaria text includes a 2017 notice; obtain current health-authority advice rather than reproducing medication guidance.
